sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: India’s New Education Policy (NEP) represents a paradigmatic departure from the colonial legacy of rote memorization toward a holistic, multidisciplinary framework. By restructuring the pedagogical hierarchy from 10+2 to a 5+3+3+4 system, the policy aims to integrate vocational skills with academic rigor, thereby dissolving the rigid silos between arts, sciences, and commerce. The emphasis on mother-tongue instruction in foundational years acknowledges the cognitive benefits of learning in a native language. However, the grandeur of the vision faces the friction of ground realities. The "implementation gap" poses a severe threat; a multidisciplinary approach requires teachers capable of traversing disciplinary boundaries—a resource currently scarce. Without a massive overhaul of infrastructure and teacher training, the NEP risks remaining a visionary document.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Tourism in India is often promoted as a vital instrument of economic growth and cultural exchange. Heritage monuments, religious destinations, and natural landscapes attract large numbers of domestic and international visitors. Revenue from tourism generates employment and supports local economies. However, unchecked tourism places immense pressure on fragile ecosystems and historical sites. Cultural practices are frequently modified to suit tourist expectations, reducing living traditions to staged performances. Infrastructure development prioritizes visitor convenience while overlooking local environmental limits. Seasonal tourist influxes strain water supply, waste management, and transport systems. Local communities often have limited participation in planning and decision-making. As a result, economic benefits coexist with cultural erosion and environmental degradation. Sustainable tourism therefore requires balancing economic objectives with ecological responsibility and cultural integrity.

questions.q: The "5+3+3+4 system" mentioned in the passage refers to:
opts: The number of languages a student must learn.
The years needed for a PhD.
The new structure of school education.
questions.why: Detail: it replaces the 10+2 'pedagogical hierarchy'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The primary objective of the NEP, as described, is to:
opts: Shift from rote learning to a multidisciplinary, holistic framework.
Separate arts, sciences and commerce more rigidly.
questions.why: Main idea: the first sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: What is identified as the major challenge to the NEP?
opts: The scarcity of teachers able to teach across disciplines.
Students' lack of interest in vocational skills.
Refusal to use the mother tongue.
questions.why: Detail: the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The phrase "dissolving the rigid silos" means:
opts: Breaking down the strict separation between streams of study.
questions.why: Vocabulary in context: silos between 'arts, sciences, and commerce'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: Why does the policy emphasize mother-tongue instruction?
opts: Because of the cognitive benefits of learning in one's native language.
English is too hard for children.
questions.why: Detail: the third sentence. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Civil Registrar-cum-Sub Registrar), Mar 2026.

questions.q: The central concern of the passage is the
opts: imbalance between tourism growth and sustainability
lack of cultural diversity at tourist sites
decline of tourist interest in India
questions.why: Main idea: benefits 'coexist with cultural erosion and environmental degradation'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Professor in Pharmaceutics), Jan 2026.

questions.q: Choose the correct sentence:
opts: This hospital is more better equipped than any other hospital in the district.
This hospital is better equipped than any hospital in the district.
This hospital is best equipped than any other hospital in the district.
This hospital is better equipped than any other hospital in the district.
questions.why: Comparing one member with the rest of its own group needs 'any other'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the error: “The furnitures in the new ward were donated by a trust.”
questions.why: 'Furniture' is uncountable: 'The furniture … was donated'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct passive construction: “People expect the minister to resign.”
opts: The minister is expected to resign.
It is expected the minister to resign.
questions.why: The same pattern as GPSC's 2026 items: subject + is expected + to-infinitive. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “When I was young, I ______ swim across the river.”
questions.why: 'Could' expresses ability in the past. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the word opposite in meaning to “ephemeral”:
questions.why: Ephemeral = lasting a very short time. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: According to a NITI Aayog report (2026), about how many Indian youth aged 15–29 are 'NEET' (not in education, employment or training)?
The theme of Rashtriya Poshan Maah 2026, its ninth edition, was:
Who was Player of the Match when India beat Sri Lanka by 165 runs in the Galle Test (August 2026)?
India won the Men's Junior Asia Cup and retained the Women's Junior Asia Cup in 2026. Junior Asia Cups are age-group tournaments in:
World Animal Welfare Day is observed on:
questions.why: Feast day of St Francis of Assisi.

questions.q: The Shri Mangueshi temple is in which taluka of Goa?
questions.why: At Priol, Ponda.

questions.q: India's real GVA growth for April–June 2026 (Q1 FY27) was:
questions.why: GDP growth was 7.8%. Aug 2026.

questions.q: ISRO tested the semi-cryogenic pre-burner for its SCE-200 engine in October 2026 at:
questions.why: ISRO Propulsion Complex.

questions.q: Anant Nag, who received the Dadasaheb Phalke Award for 2024, is known mainly for films in:
questions.why: Presented in September 2026.

questions.q: The Battle of Plassey was fought in:
questions.why: Robert Clive defeated Siraj-ud-Daulah.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 8, 27, 64, 125, ?
questions.why: These are the cubes of 2, 3, 4 and 5. The next is 6 cubed, 216.

questions.q: Which letter is exactly midway between G and S in the English alphabet?
questions.why: G is the 7th letter and S the 19th. Midway is the 13th letter, M.

questions.q: If CLERK is written as DMFSL in a certain code, how is JUDGE written?
questions.why: Each letter moves one place forward: J-K, U-V, D-E, G-H, E-F.

questions.q: Thermometer is to temperature as seismograph is to:
questions.why: A seismograph records the ground movement caused by earthquakes.

questions.q: Q and R are brother and sister. P is Q's son and S is R's son. How is P related to S?
questions.why: The children of a brother and a sister are cousins.

questions.q: Starting from point X, Raju walks 6 km north, then 8 km east, then 6 km south. How far is he from X?
questions.why: The 6 km north and 6 km south cancel out, leaving him 8 km east of X.

questions.q: A, B and C can do a work in 20, 30 and 60 days. In how many days can A do it if B and C help him every third day?
questions.why: Per 3 days: 3/20 + 1/30 + 1/60 = 12/60 = 1/5 of the work, so 15 days. GPSC CBRT, Mar 2025.

questions.q: Which word does NOT belong with the others?
questions.why: The first three mean 'of little importance'. GPSC CBRT, Sep 2025.

questions.q: Statement: "The government should immediately tighten regulation of pharmaceutical advertising to protect public health." Which assumption is inherent?
opts: Such advertising now misleads the public or poses a health risk
Regulation is the only way to protect public health
The government has all the resources needed
Public health is deteriorating because of such advertising
questions.why: The call for urgent regulation presumes a present risk. B and D are too strong. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: Identify the next term: 1, 2, 6, 42, 1806, …
questions.why: Each term is n × (n + 1) of the previous: 1806 × 1807 = 3263442. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: According to §83, the physician taking the case needs above all:
opts: laboratory reports before speaking to the patient
freedom from prejudice, sound senses, attention in observing and fidelity in recording
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §83: the unprejudiced observer; case taking demands freedom from prejudice and sound senses.

questions.q: According to §18, the sole indication guiding the choice of the remedy is:
opts: the totality of symptoms, with its accompanying circumstances
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §18: the sum of all the symptoms and circumstances is the sole indication.

questions.q: After the first prescription the patient is steadily improving. The right course is to:
opts: wait, and not repeat or change while improvement continues
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. A remedy that is acting is left alone. Kent: when in doubt, wait.

questions.q: Discharges with a fish-brine odour are characteristic of which miasm?
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. Offensive, fish-brine discharges are a sycotic keynote.

questions.q: A patient who is very awkward, drops things, with puffiness and a tendency for marks to persist after pressure from scissors or instruments, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Bovista: awkwardness, deep imprints from blunt instruments.

questions.q: Extreme weakness from the heat of the sun, with great debility, inability to digest milk and sensitivity to music, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Natrum carb: worse from summer heat and mental exertion.

questions.q: An organ remedy used in mother tincture for left-sided splenic enlargement and pain is:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Ceanothus is the classic spleen remedy.

questions.q: Which remedy is complementary to Pulsatilla?
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Silicea is the chronic of Pulsatilla; Kali sulph is also complementary.

questions.q: Under the old Hahnemannian method, mother tinctures were prepared in different classes according to:
opts: the juice and moisture content of the plant (Classes I to IX)
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. The new HPI method uses a uniform drug strength.

questions.q: 'Strong alcohol' in the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India is ethanol of about:
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Weaker alcohols are diluted from it.

questions.q: Guernsey's repertory dealing only with haemorrhoids is an example of a:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. W. J. Guernsey's 'Haemorrhoids' (also Bell's Diarrhoea).

questions.q: The correct order of the steps after case taking is:
opts: analysis and evaluation of symptoms, totality, repertorisation, then final selection from the materia medica
materia medica first, then case taking
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. The repertory narrows the field; the materia medica decides.

questions.q: The normal PR interval on the ECG is:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. It mainly reflects conduction delay in the AV node.

questions.q: The normal serum anion gap is about:
questions.why: Topic 5, Anatomy and Physiology. Raised in diabetic ketoacidosis, lactic acidosis, renal failure and some poisonings.

questions.q: Red blood cell casts in urine indicate:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. WBC casts suggest pyelonephritis.

questions.q: Blunting of the costophrenic angle on a chest X-ray suggests:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Fluid collects first in the costophrenic recess; at least 200 mL on a PA film.

questions.q: Recurrent abdominal pain related to defecation, with altered stool frequency or form and no structural disease, is:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Rome IV criteria for IBS; a functional disorder.

questions.q: Asterixis (flapping tremor) in a cirrhotic patient suggests:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Also seen in CO2 retention and uraemia.

questions.q: The usual HbA1c target for most adults with diabetes is below:
questions.why: Topic 7, Practice of Medicine. Targets are individualised; 7% suits most adults.

questions.q: The commonest benign tumour of the uterus, a frequent cause of heavy menstrual bleeding, is the:
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Fibroids are smooth-muscle tumours; they cause menorrhagia and infertility.

questions.q: The commonest cause of infantile diarrhoea worldwide is (GPSC Medical Officer, 2024):
questions.why: Topic 8, Obstetrics, Gynaecology and Paediatrics. Rotavirus vaccine is in India's UIP.

questions.q: Fractures that are slow to unite, with pricking pain at the site, are helped by:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Symphytum ('knitbone') promotes union of fractures.

questions.q: After a clean surgical incision, with smarting pain and a sense of insult, the remedy usually indicated is:
questions.why: Topic 9, Surgery, ENT, Eye and First Aid. Staphysagria: clean-cut wounds and post-operative pain.

questions.q: Under the MTP (Amendment) Act 2021, the opinion of two registered doctors is needed for termination at (GPSC Medical Officer, 2025):
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. One doctor up to 20 weeks; a medical board beyond 24 weeks for fetal anomalies.

questions.q: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) consists of:
opts: infant mortality, literacy and life expectancy at age one
questions.why: Topic 10, Community and Forensic Medicine, Ethics. As keyed in GPSC Medical Officer, 2024.
